plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 41: Atomic Structure
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a two-dimensional vector diagram of the allowed orientations of an orbital angular momentum vector. A vertical axis labeled z rises from an origin set at the left of the frame and is crossed there by an unlabeled horizontal axis. Seven olive-green arrows of identical length fan out from the origin into the right half of the plane, their tips landing on a dashed circular arc that makes their common magnitude explicit; the topmost arrow is labeled L with a vector arrow. A dashed horizontal line runs from each tip back to the z axis, which is ticked and labeled from top to bottom 3ħ, 2ħ, ħ, then the unlabeled origin, then -ħ, -2ħ, and -3ħ, so the arrows step in equal increments of z component rather than in equal angles. Four thin arcs of increasing radius sweep from the positive z axis to the four upper arrows and are labeled θ0 nearest the origin, then θ1, θ2, and θ3; the θ0 arc opens all the way to the horizontal arrow while the θ3 arc closes on the steepest one. Holding the arrow length fixed while stepping the projections in equal units shows that only a discrete set of polar angles is available to the vector.

elements: flat 2D vertical z-axis at the left, with an arrowhead at the top and label z above it
flat 2D horizontal axis crossing the origin, extending left a short distance and right past the longest arrow tip
origin point where all angular momentum vectors begin
z-axis tick marks at +3ħ, +2ħ, +ħ, -ħ, -2ħ, and -3ħ, with labels on the left side of the axis
seven olive-green angular momentum arrows L radiating from the origin into the right half-plane for m = -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3
all seven L arrows having the same length and tips lying on one dashed circular arc
dashed circular arc through the vector tips, centered at the origin, showing constant |L|
horizontal dashed projection guide lines from each nonzero vector tip back to the z-axis at Lz = mħ
top/right vector label L with an over-arrow
four thin angle arcs centered at the origin in the upper quadrant, measuring polar angle from the positive z-axis to the upper allowed vectors
angle labels θ0, θ1, θ2, θ3 placed beside the corresponding arcs
optional faint continuous fan of many possible L directions, visible only in continuous-angle mode

interactions.label: Allowed m value
interactions.teaches: Each allowed orientation has a z component fixed to Lz = mħ, while every vector keeps the same total angular momentum length

interactions.label: Angles
interactions.teaches: The orbital angular momentum vector is not free to point at every polar angle; only the orientations whose z projections match integer multiples of ħ are allowed

interactions.label: Orbital quantum number l
interactions.teaches: Changing l changes both the common vector magnitude |L| = sqrt(l(l+1))ħ and the number of allowed projection states, 2l + 1

demo_steps.title: Highest projection
demo_steps.narration: For l = 3, the uppermost vector has m = 3, so its dashed guide lands on Lz = 3ħ. The arrow is long but steep because its z component is close to the total magnitude.

demo_steps.title: Zero projection
demo_steps.narration: At m = 0, the vector points horizontally. Its length has not changed, but its z component is zero.

demo_steps.title: Lowest projection
demo_steps.narration: At m = -3, the vector has the same length as before but projects to -3ħ on the z-axis. The quantization is in the vertical projection, not in the vector length.

demo_steps.title: Change l
demo_steps.narration: Reducing l to 2 shortens the common radius to sqrt(6)ħ and leaves only five allowed projections, m = -2 through +2.

demo_steps.title: Compare with continuous angles
demo_steps.narration: The faint fan shows all the directions that would be possible classically. Switching back to the discrete view reveals the selected quantum orientations.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a flat 2D world coordinate system with +X screen-right and +Y screen-up; the plotted vertical coordinate is z in units of ħ. Default source figure is l = 3, so |L| = sqrt(l(l+1))ħ = sqrt(12)ħ ≈ 3.464ħ. Place the origin at (0, 0). The z-axis is the vertical line x = 0 from y = -3.45 to y = 3.75, with a black arrowhead at the top and label z above y ≈ 3.85. The horizontal axis is y = 0 from x = -1.05 to x = 3.95. For default l = 3, draw seven equal-length olive arrows from the origin to tips: m = 3 at (1.732, 3), m = 2 at (2.828, 2), m = 1 at (3.317, 1), m = 0 at (3.464, 0), m = -1 at (3.317, -1), m = -2 at (2.828, -2), and m = -3 at (1.732, -3). General formula for slider l: R = sqrt(l(l+1)); allowed m are all integers -l ≤ m ≤ l; each arrow tip is (sqrt(R^2 - m^2), m). For l = 0, show only a small zero-length marker at the origin and the label m = 0. Dashed horizontal projection lines run from x = 0 to the selected/default arrow-tip x value at y = m for all nonzero allowed m; use grey/black dashed strokes. The dashed circular arc is the right-hand arc of the circle x^2 + y^2 = R^2, drawn only over the vertical range y ∈ [-l, l], so it passes through all arrow tips. Tick labels on the z-axis update to ±ħ, ±2ħ, ... ±lħ; the source labels for l = 3 are 3ħ, 2ħ, ħ, -ħ, -2ħ, -3ħ. Arrow color is olive green, approximately #78a22f; selected arrow should be brighter/thicker, around #6fa128, while unselected arrows can be slightly thinner or lower opacity. Axes and text are black #111111; dashed construction lines are dark grey #555555. Angle arcs are centered at the origin and measured clockwise from the positive z-axis to the upper arrows. In the l = 3 source view, show θ0 from +z to the horizontal m = 0 arrow at radius about 0.55, θ1 to m = 1 at radius about 0.95, θ2 to m = 2 at radius about 1.35, and θ3 to m = 3 at radius about 1.75; label each arc near its middle. The L vector label sits near the upper-right allowed vector region, just to the right of the m = 2 or m = 3 arrow tip cluster.
interactionPlan.notes: Render as an orthographic 2D scene using Three.js lines, arrowheads, dashed LineSegments, and CSS2D/SDF text labels. Keep the original figure composition: z-axis on the left, vectors fanning to the right, labels outside the dashed guides. The allowedM control should only enable or visibly cycle through states with |m| ≤ l; if l changes and the current m becomes invalid, clamp to the nearest valid m. In discrete mode, show all allowed arrows for the current l, with one highlighted according to allowedM. In continuous fan mode, replace or strongly fade the discrete arrows and draw many faint radial directions of the same radius R across the same right-hand angular span, so the contrast with the discrete quantum states is visually clear.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Button / state for allowed m values: the learner steps through m = -3 to 3, one green L vector highlights at a time and its dashed projection lands on the matching hbar tick, showing that the z component is quantized while the vector length stays fixed.

authoredContext:
The quantization of the polar angle for the l=3 state is shown in the figure. The orbital angular momentum vector lies somewhere on the surface of a cone with an opening angle θ relative to the z-axis (unless m=0, in which case θ=90° and the vector points are perpendicular to the z-axis).

The quantization of orbital angular momentum. Each vector lies on the surface of a cone with axis along the z-axis.

Seven vector, all of the same length L, are drawn at 7 different angles to the z axis. The z components of the vectors are indicated both by horizontal lines from the tip of the vector to the z axis and by labels on the z axis. For four of the vectors, the angle between the z axis and the vector is also labeled. The z component values are 3 h bar at angle theta sub three, 2 h bar at angle theta sub two, h bar at angle theta sub one, zero at angle theta sub zero, minus h bar, minus 2 h bar, and minus 3 h bar.

A detailed study of angular momentum reveals that we cannot know all three components simultaneously. In the previous section, the z-component of orbital angular momentum has definite values that depend on the quantum number m. This implies that we cannot know both x- and y-components of angular momentum, Lx and Ly, with certainty. As a result, the precise direction of the orbital angular momentum vector is unknown.

discrepancies: The source shows all seven green L vectors with essentially equal visual weight, while the generated figure highlights the m=3 vector as thicker/brighter by default.
The vector label renders as 'L□' rather than a clean L with an over-arrow as in the source.
The horizontal axis in the source extends much farther across the figure, while the generated version is noticeably shortened on the left and right.
The angle-arc labeling is somewhat ambiguous and may not match the source ordering/placement of θ0 through θ3 exactly.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable and conceptually strong, but the default selected-arrow emphasis and imperfect vector-label rendering reduce fidelity to the static source.
action_items: Make all seven green vectors equal thickness and opacity in the default view, or make the selection highlight less visually dominant.
Replace the broken L vector glyph with a reliably rendered label such as bold L with a CSS/HTML over-arrow.
Extend the horizontal axis farther left and right to better match the source composition.
Check and adjust θ0–θ3 label placement so their ordering and association with the angle arcs matches the original figure.
